info.name: Agent tool-call authorization matrix (Phase 9)
info.description: The AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ slice proven end to end through the gateway, with the collection itself as a deterministic scripted MCP client (streamable HTTP, POST /mcp: `initialize` answers plain application/json and assigns Mcp-Session-Id as a response header; `notifications/initialized` answers 202 with an empty body; every later request is SSE-framed). Cells E1–E11 of docs/to-do/implemented/AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ/10-QA-TEST-CASES.md, plus E12 (MCP-AUTH-LIBRARY: the agent-clients guard) and E13/E15 (GATEWAY-AUDIENCE-BINDING: the protected-resource documents, and the MCP host agent minted by the discovery login), and E17 (the transport's own refusals carry no stack trace). Every assertion is on the actual cut — which tool names, which denials, which LAYER — never on response shape alone. E6 (PDP kill), E7 (agent-gate off), E11 (revocation) and E12 (agent-clients guard) are drills the runner orchestrates around the rig: run this collection with scripts/postman/run-agent-tool-matrix.sh, not standalone.

exec: // One deterministic MCP client, written as Postman scripts. Postman has no module system, so
// the shared streamable-HTTP framing helpers live in a collection variable and are eval'd by

"    return { isError: result.isError === true, layer: meta.layer || null,",
"             code: meta.code || null, text: text, json: parsed };",
"// E8: every deny is a STRUCTURED tool error naming its layer and a stable code \u2014 never a",
